title: JRA-3Q marine 2 m air warms half as fast as its SST in 1980-2022 because daytime ocean analysis increments decrease; its global trend is 16-21% low, and its 1985 SST switch adds +0.08 C
abstract: We test the surface temperature record of the JMA reanalysis JRA-3Q, one of the data sets in WMO global temperature assessments. We use JRA-3Q monthly and diurnal statistics (1975-2026), the JMA twin run JRA-3Q-COBE (June 1985-December 1990), ERA5, five SST products, CLASSnmat night marine air temperature, Berkeley Earth and NOAAGlobalTemp. Over ice-free ocean (60S-60N), JRA-3Q analysed 2 m temperature (T2m) warms 0.071 C per decade in 1980-2022, but its SST boundary warms 0.138 and its own model first guess 0.137 C per decade. ERA5 marine T2m warms 1.06 times its SST. The ocean analysis increment (analysis minus first guess) falls from +0.45 C in the 1980s to about +0.2 C after 2010 (-0.066 C per decade). The increment is mostly a daytime signal (+0.88 C at local noon, +0.11 C at midnight in the 1980s), and about 80% of its decrease is in daytime. This agrees with solar heating of ship air temperature sensors and a smaller weight of ship reports with time; we did not count the observations. As a result, the published JRA-3Q global-mean T2m warms 0.153 C per decade in 1980-2022, 0.030-0.040 C per decade (16-21%) less than Berkeley Earth, ERA5 and NOAAGlobalTemp. With the first guess over the ocean, the trend becomes 0.186-0.192 C per decade and agrees with them. Separately, the JRA-3Q SST boundary rises by +0.084 C (60S-60N) at the June 1985 change from COBE-SST2 to MGDSST; the twin run gives +0.081 C. MGDSST also has transient cold periods (1992-93, 2002-03, 2021-22). In the twin run the analysed marine T2m keeps only 27% of the SST change, so the boundary step barely reaches T2m. Limitations: the first-guess replacement is a diagnostic, not a product, and is 0.03-0.05 C warm in 2023-2024; the cause of the increment decrease is an inference from its day-night pattern; the twin covers only 1985-1990. No third-party data are in the bundle; scripts regenerate all numbers.

display.caption: Published JRA-3Q global-mean 2 m temperature (red) is about 0.1 C too warm before 1991 relative to Berkeley Earth, ERA5 and NOAAGlobalTemp; its 1980-2022 trend is 16-21% low. Using the JRA-3Q model first guess over the ocean removes the deficit.
Ice-free ocean 60S-60N: the JRA-3Q model first guess follows the SST boundary, but the analysed T2m does not; the analysis increment falls by about 0.25 C from the 1980s to the 2010s.
The ocean T2m analysis increment is large at local noon and afternoon and small at night; most of its decrease from 1980-1989 to 2010-2019 is in daytime.
